summary: Same blink-and-fade rainbow sparkle with a near-identical 0.8 s fade and identical average blink budget, but the port reacts on only every OTHER beat (1 Hz mass relight of ~40/60 pixels, then ~0.45 s with zero new blinks) where the original blinks continuously on every frame at a beat-modulated rate — so the port strobes to near-black and reads near-monochrome while the original is a continuous multi-hue shimmer.
observations: Control surface: both sides expose ZERO controls (meta.json sides.orig.controls == sides.port.controls == []). --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on both. No control-surface mismatch.

Both sides are fully sound-gated: with --sensors off (--skip 100 --seconds 8 --fps 20, label sens-off) BOTH render mean brightness 0 / motion 0. Both report wantsSensors:true and were fed sensors:'synth' sensorModel:'beat120' in every judged run.

BEAT CADENCE (the headline divergence). 40 s window at 20 fps (label fps20-40s), autocorrelation of the motion series: orig lag10 (0.5 s) = 0.59, lag20 (1.0 s) = 0.62, lag30 = 0.70, lag40 = 0.59 -> responds on EVERY 2 Hz beat. Port: lag10 (0.5 s) = 0.07, lag20 (1.0 s) = 0.83, lag30 (1.5 s) = 0.11, lag40 (2.0 s) = 0.87 -> responds only every OTHER beat, at 1 Hz. Reproduced at 10 fps (orig top lag 1.5 s, port 1.0 s), 20 fps and 40 fps (orig 0.50 s, port 1.00 s), so it is not an fps or aliasing artefact.

BLINK DISTRIBUTION (root of the cadence difference). Newly-lit-pixel count per frame over a 40 s window at 10 fps (label huetrack, pixel value rising by >8): orig avg 12.6/frame, range 6-22, ZERO frames with no new blinks (0.0%). Port avg 12.7/frame — the same total budget — but delivered as a mass event of 40-52 pixels once per second followed by exactly 4-5 frames (~0.45 s) of ZERO new blinks, then a ramp (3,11,18,18,26 ...) into the next mass event; 40.4% of port frames have no new blink at all. Confirmed frame-by-frame at 20 fps (label decay, t=200-202 s): port newly-lit = 39 at t=200.55, then 0 for t=200.60..201.00 (9 consecutive frames), then 7-14/frame for t=201.05..201.50, then 41 at t=201.55.

STROBING / BLACK GAPS. Same 40 s / 20 fps window, meanBrightness percentiles: orig p5=11, p25=18, p50=24, p75=31, p95=42, min 6, max 57; port p5=4, p25=9, p50=24, p75=38, p95=57, min 2, max 85. Frames below mean brightness 8: orig 0.4%, port 22.6%. Below 15: orig 13.9%, port 35.9%. Medians are identical (24) — the port has the right average and the wrong dynamic range: it flashes twice as hard and falls to near-black between flashes, the original never goes dark. Visible directly in the grid16 rhythm images: the original's hue bands run into each other continuously, the port's are separated by black gaps.

FADE ENVELOPE MATCHES. Tracking individual pixels from 255 down (label decay, 20 fps, 13 orig / 14 port traces): time from full brightness to below 8 is 16.3 frames = 0.82 s on the original and 15.9 frames = 0.80 s on the port. Curve shape differs slightly: orig decays geometrically from the outset (255 -> 238,203,170,140,113,89,68,50,34,22,12,5, ratio ~0.83/frame), port holds near full for a few frames then falls almost linearly (~ -17/frame: 255,241,223,206,189,173,156,139) before accelerating to zero. Minor.

HUE WALK. Both sides walk a global hue continuously through the full rainbow, same direction, fps-invariant. Measured by unwrapping the hue of the brightest pixel over 40 s (label huetrack) and cross-checked from mean-colour hue at 10/20/40 fps: orig 0.218 cyc/s (period 4.59 s), port 0.189-0.191 cyc/s (period 5.30 s). The port's hue cycle is ~13-15% SLOW. Rates were identical at 10, 20 and 40 fps on both sides (orig 0.217/0.218/0.218, port 0.189/0.191/0.189) — no frame-rate coupling in steady state on either side.

HUE DIVERSITY ON THE STRIP. Each pixel latches the hue current at its blink and keeps it while fading, on BOTH sides — but because the original blinks continuously it always carries a smear of history: avg 6.6 distinct hues (2 dp) among ~30-45 lit pixels per frame, spanning ~0.15-0.20 of hue (e.g. t=200.00 s, orig lit hues span 0.571..0.754). The port averages only 2.6 distinct hues per frame and is exactly monochrome for the whole post-mass-event half of its cycle (e.g. t=200.65..201.00 s every lit pixel is hue 0.304-0.313, circular concentration 1.000). Net effect: original reads as a multicolour rainbow sparkle, port as a single-colour strobe whose colour steps each cycle.

ORIGINAL WARM-UP TRANSIENT, ABSENT IN THE PORT. The original opens with an all-yellow full-brightness strip (baseline t=0-6 s: meanBrightness avg 139, min 125, motion avg 1.7, meanR 202 / meanG 183 / meanB 33 — nearly static), which turns into a dense full-brightness rainbow chaos (label mode-warmup, mean 90) and only thins into the sparse sparkle after roughly 450 RENDERED FRAMES. It is frame-counted, not time-based: settles at t~45 s at 10 fps, t~22 s at 20 fps, t~11 s at 40 fps (labels warm-f10/warm-f20/warm-f40, 5 s bins). The port has no such transient — it is at its steady mean of ~25 within a few seconds at every fps. On real hardware at 60-100 fps the original's opening flash would last ~5-8 s.

STEADY STATE (t >= 100 s, labels steady100 / steady200 / mode-transition) is where both sides live and where the comparison above was made: both settle at meanBrightness ~25 and stay there indefinitely (300 s survey: orig 25-27 per 10 s bin from t=50 to t=300, port 23-27 from t=20 to t=300). Neither side dies, saturates or drifts; brightnessTrend 'volatile' on both is the beat, not decay.

STOCHASTIC CHARACTER IS SEED- AND RIG-STABLE. Seeds 1, 7 and 1234 at t=100 s give orig mean 26/26/26 motion 10/10/10 and port 27/26/27 motion 7/7/7 — the divergence is not a one-seed fluke. Re-rendering on --pixels 300 and on --rig grid --grid 16x16 reproduces the same stats and the same qualitative difference, so it is not a rig artefact either.
feedback: Fix the beat response first: the port fires one mass blink per 1.0 s (every other beat of the 2 Hz beat120 feed) whereas the original blinks on every beat. Target: motion-series autocorrelation should peak at 0.5 s (10 frames at 20 fps), not 1.0 s. Whatever gates the port's blink appears to have a ~0.45 s refractory/hold after firing — that hold has to go.

Change the blink from an all-at-once event to a continuous per-frame trickle. The original lights 6-22 fresh pixels EVERY rendered frame (avg 12.6/frame at 10 fps, never zero), with that rate swelling and shrinking with the audio envelope. The port lights 40-52 at once and then nothing for 4-5 frames. Same total budget, wrong distribution: it should be a per-frame blink probability scaled by the audio level, not a threshold trigger.

Consequence to verify after that fix: the strip must never go dark. Original's mean brightness stays above 8 in 99.6% of frames (p5 = 11); the port currently drops below 8 in 22.6% of frames (min 2) and peaks nearly twice as high (max 85 vs 57). Aim for the original's tighter distribution p5 11 / p50 24 / p95 42 rather than the port's 4 / 24 / 57.

Because blinking is continuous on the original, several hues are visible at once (avg 6.6 distinct hues per frame, spanning ~0.15-0.20 of the hue wheel). The port is monochrome for half of every cycle (avg 2.6 distinct hues, exactly one hue for ~0.45 s at a time). Fixing the blink distribution should fix this automatically — the hue latching itself is already correct on both sides.
Speed the hue walk up by ~15%: the original completes a full rainbow in 4.59 s, the port in 5.30 s (measured over 40 s, identical at 10/20/40 fps).

The fade is already right — leave it alone. Full brightness to invisible takes 0.82 s on the original and 0.80 s on the port. Optional nitpick: the original's fade is geometric from the first frame (~x0.83 per frame at 20 fps) while the port holds near full for 2-3 frames then falls roughly linearly (~ -17/frame) before accelerating.

Low priority: the original has a ~450-RENDERED-FRAME warm-up (all pixels yellow at full brightness, then a saturated full-brightness rainbow, thinning into the sparkle) that the port does not reproduce at all — the port starts at steady state. Frame-counted, so ~22 s at 20 fps and ~7 s on hardware. Worth matching only after the rhythm is fixed; a viewer watching for a minute sees the steady state, not this.
